js: src/game.js (world.damageHit/nearWindow/blastWindows/punchHole/stripPropsAt/igniteBlast/blastDebris/onShake, src/ballistics.js classifySurface's world hooks, src/breakup.js's world hooks)
note: Implements Combat/CombatWorldHooks.cs's IDamageWorld + Combat/Ballistics.cs's IBallisticsWorld + Combat/AirframeBreakup.cs's IBreakupWorld as ONE adapter against the live TerrainSampler/building-chunk/Fx/AudioFx systems, then Install(GameLoop) wires everything GameLoop.cs's own class header lists as a named, unassigned hook: constructs FireSystem/ImpactFx/BreakingGlass/PlaneDamage/MachineGun/RocketLauncher/BlastFx/BulletSim/HeldWeapon and appends them to GameLoop.CombatSystems in game.js:2440-2460's order (minus smoke/planephys/breakup/dents/paper/lanes/fire, which are either ticked elsewhere already or genuinely out of this scope -- documented per-stage); assigns GameLoop.CrashFactory (wraps Core/CrashSequence.cs + a per-plane PlaneDamageRecord's real Size); assigns GameLoop.Terrain/Boundary/Zones (CityData.Load/BoundaryWall.Load/ZoneBuilder.Load -- nobody built these at runtime before); assigns GameLoop.WorldTick to a City/CityCulling.cs instance's Tick(camPos,dt) (an exact Action<Vector3,float> match that showed up mid-task); closes the IsArmedProvider/OnToggleAim/OnTakePickup/OnGoAirport hooks (the last folds goAirport()+_parkInShed() into one H-key toggle keyed off distance to GameLoop.ShedSpawnPos, using AirportBuilder's real OSM runway polyline via GeoFrame.FromLatLon for the airport half); registers every PlaneDamageRecord in the scene into GameLoop.Targets (GameLoop.cs:962's Register() had ZERO callers anywhere in the 165-file project before this -- the parked fleet/own-plane target card, the Tab cycle and the 'sheni manqana' [your vehicle] Sub label were all dead code as a result) and into PlaneDamage.Watch(); attaches the UI Toolkit panel (HudView/SkillBarView/WeaponBarView -- parameterless VisualElement ctors -- plus SettingsView/TargetCardView/UI.Credits.CreditsView, each cloning its real Assets/UI/*/*.uxml, closing the 'never wired into any scene' gap those three views' own headers flagged; MapUiRoot stays unwired, needs map textures+district/subzone polygons on top of a UXML, documented not silent). HONEST GAPS, stated in the file's own header: no per-window glass on buildings (BuildingBuilder.cs's walls are flat quads, no window cells -- NearWindow/BlastWindows always answer false/empty); no BreakWall.cs hole-carving/prop-stripping (needs a chunk-positional-index -> original-building-index mapping BuildingBuilder.Chunk does not expose, and reconstructing BuildingBuilder's own cell-grouping/skip logic from outside City/ without a compiler was judged too risky); IsDestructible/IsLandmark/IsRoadSurface always false (no such tags exist anywhere in City/ yet -- SurfaceClassifier's material-name fallback already carries most real cases). What IS real: a building loses real HP per hit, addressed to the exact Chunk.Ranges vertex range BuildingBuilder.cs's own class doc calls the addressing unit, and visibly crumbles (CombatBuildingChunk: darkens + sinks that range, 10 stages) -- not the JS's full hole system, but genuine per-building damage, not a stub. CombatBuildingChunk's MeshCollider is never recooked per hit (documented, bounded: post-collapse hit tests land slightly proud of the visible crumble, never through it). Also defines CombatTerrainTag (a bare marker MonoBehaviour) and FxSink (IFireFx+IImpactSink, forwarding to Fx/FireSystem.cs + Core/AudioFx.cs's FxAudio + Combat/ImpactFx.cs's shared Debris/Sparks pools) and the nested PlayableSceneBoot MonoBehaviour -- the no-login-UI/server stand-in for Boot.cs's real StartFlightAsync, called by both Editor/BuildPlayableScene.cs's saved scene and Editor/Probes/PlayableProbe.cs. REVISED after first probe run (3 PASS/4 FAIL: combatSystemsOverFour/crashFactoryAssigned/heroBodyExists/uiPanelPresent all failed together, STARTED_BEFORE_TICKS=False, LAST_STAGE_COUNT=1): Install() previously ran start-to-finish with no isolation, so one early, uncaught exception could silently take every downstream phase down with it (and a probe-side try/catch around the whole call site would hide exactly which line). Install() is now split into independent try/catch phases (terrain, boundary, zones, the big combat-system construction block, WorldTick/CityCulling, InstallUi) -- a failure in one no longer blocks the others, and each catch logs via Debug.LogException. Also: PlayableSceneBoot moved OUT of being nested inside CombatWorldAdapter to a top-level class in the same file/namespace (removes a plausible AddComponent/FindObjectByType risk factor outright rather than arguing it was fine) and its own Run() got the same four-phase isolation (Init/Install/body-spawn/BeginSession). Two one-line diagnostic summaries added (COMBATWORLDADAPTER installed.../PLAYABLESCENEBOOT ran...) so the next log review does not need to hunt through 300 ticks of output. [COORDINATOR 2026-10-27 MonoBehaviour split] Core/CombatWorldAdapter.cs declared THREE MonoBehaviours (CombatTerrainTag, CombatBuildingChunk, PlayableSceneBoot) in a file named after a non-MonoBehaviour class. Unity cannot bind a script asset to a MonoBehaviour whose file is not named after it, so AddComponent produced components serialised with `m_Script: {fileID: 187830060}` and NO guid. PlayableProbe failed playableSceneBootExists on a freshly-built scene that contained both the named GameObject and 605 chunks of baked RangeStart data — the YAML was present, the live component was not, Install() never ran, and CombatSystems/CrashFactory/hero/UI all read missing together. Split into Core/CombatTerrainTag.cs, Core/CombatBuildingChunk.cs and Core/PlayableSceneBoot.cs; CombatWorldAdapter.cs went 1207 -> 703 lines. After a rebuild the scene binds properly (m_Script fileID 11500000 + a real guid; 605 chunk refs, 49 terrain tags, 1 boot). Rule now in the project skill.
